# Product conformance status

This matrix is the repository-wide source of truth for the unpublished
`http`, `http3`, and `quic_core` packages. `Ready` means the executable
gate exists and currently passes. `Blocked` means implementation or
release evidence is incomplete. `ExternalPending` is reserved for a
condition that cannot be produced by this unpublished worktree.

| ID | Area | Status | Current evidence or required next gate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PROD-001 | Three-package ownership | `Ready` | Executable layout and compiler-interface audits enforce `http -> http3 -> quic_core` and reject the former package path. |
| PROD-002 | Common body and error types | `Blocked` | Bounded body and common error tests now include supervised cleanup, exact concurrent cleanup outcomes, and separate source EOF, final wire result, and resource-release observations. Current-source full qualification and cross-protocol negative-case coverage remain required. |
| PROD-003 | Regression baselines | `Blocked` | Source discovery finds 1240 root, 488 HTTP/3, and 648 QUIC core tests. Native Windows reproduced the original 14 failures before fixes. The updated source must complete the independent three-package OS/OTP matrix and canonical-source verification before this baseline is Ready. |
| PROD-004 | Public-only HTTP/3-to-QUIC boundary | `Ready` | The private import allowlist contains 0 entries; source scan, compiler-interface audit, and compiled xref all reject any HTTP/3 dependency on `quic_core/internal/**`. |
| PROD-005 | Isolation and admission | `Blocked` | Grant-before-growth memory and connection admission now preserve typed memory refusal causes through retry/expiry races. New tests cover candidate socket cleanup, reciprocal connection-ID migration and retirement, pre-dial TCP admission, and shared HTTP/3 stream supervision. Full stability, hostile-peer, coverage, and platform qualification must be regenerated for the final source. |
| PROD-006 | Unified client and server | `Blocked` | The unified HTTP/3 adapter now uses public streaming APIs with concurrent supervised upload and response reception. Authenticated connection selection, non-replayable uploads, origin/endpoint separation, shared admission, and reusable connections have focused regressions. Server reservations extend through response disposal and worker termination, with separate transfer and cleanup results. Client tracing, all lifetime races, platform evidence, and final API snapshots remain under qualification. |
| PROD-007 | HTTP/1.1 runtime | `Blocked` | Strict heads/framing, verified active-once TCP/TLS paths, ordered finite pipelining, deferred Expect, half-close, pooling, and CONNECT/Upgrade streams have public tests. H1 responses now share the supervised source lifetime used for client uploads: peer TLS closure, listener stop, callback failure and deadlines cancel and join the producer. Input arriving during a pull remains bounded and preserves pipelining. Sixty-five scoped H1/TCP/TLS cases and old-server mutation controls validate the change; actual Chrome cancellation confirms source cleanup and worker exit. Listener handoff and finite phase counters remain observable. Current-source standards mapping, hostile matrices, independent-peer evidence, performance and platform qualification remain incomplete. |
| PROD-008 | HTTP/2 runtime | `Blocked` | The active-once TLS client/server runtime, explicit cleartext prior knowledge, bounded frame/HPACK/SETTINGS/flow-control/stream queues, per-stream worker isolation and deadlines, fair response scheduling, RST/GOAWAY/PING/ORIGIN/priority behavior, Extended CONNECT opt-in, graceful drain, and sequential common-pool reuse are directly tested. ORIGIN advertisements are structurally bounded, server writes are fixed to stream zero, pool authority defaults to an exact authenticated origin key, and a 421 response evicts the connection. RFC 8336 records three explicit advisory deviations because peer advertisements do not yet enable cross-origin coalescing. The hostile-peer gate passes; remaining standards mapping, interoperability, performance, and platform qualification remain open. |
| PROD-009 | HTTP/3, QUIC, TLS, and QPACK | `Blocked` | The http3 package uses public quic_core streams, with supervised streaming upload, early responses, trailers, reuse, GOAWAY and listener lifetime tests. Native connection-ID issuance, routing, retirement and migration have live regressions. QUIC admission and send backpressure retain typed memory refusal and finite diagnostic chains. Cross-group and cookie-only HelloRetryRequest, retry PSK binders and ticket age, and post-retry early-data rejection have ordinary regressions and independent mutation checks. Chrome exposed and verified fixes for asymmetric Datagram SETTINGS and response cancellation after request FIN; bounded public send-completion observation connects the three API layers. Connection admission now prepays terminal history within a 64 KiB minimum grant, and active completion waiters reserve 8 KiB before their monitors exist. Public 65535/65536-byte boundaries, caller death, actual bounded storage and terminal-error classification have ordinary and mutation controls. Final current-source suites, coverage, rejection/release matrices and QPACK/RFC evidence still require qualification. The inventory maps 39 RFCs and 1 pinned specifications; incomplete inventories are 17 RFCs and 0 pinned specifications. |
| PROD-010 | Published extensions | `Blocked` | Structured Fields, digest/signature, Binary HTTP, OHTTP, compression, WebSocket and MASQUE have bounded codecs and public behavior tests. General Brotli compressed blocks have independent synthetic-corpus comparisons. Go and TypeScript OHTTP exercise three roles, two AEADs, bodies, trailers, tampering and verified outer TLS. Independent masque-go exercises concurrent CONNECT-UDP flows, datagram association, policy rejection and joined cleanup in both roles. MASQUE has 97 scoped live and native controls, including clock overflow, owner death, reordered activity, finite contention, one-shot stop notification, confirmed idle-owner exit and typed join timeout. Four isolated mutants prove the new lifetime controls detect their target faults. Cross-platform ECN wire observations, privileged ICMP delivery, independent CONNECT-IP, final-source extension coverage and complete extension RFC maps remain incomplete. RateLimit targets the pinned draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers-11. |

RFC1950 has 13/0, RFC1951 has 11/2, RFC1952 has 13/1, RFC3986 has 0/18, RFC4648 has 4/6, RFC6265 has 52/14, RFC6455 has 164/18, RFC6797 has 34/5, RFC7239 has 22/3, RFC7301 has 10/1, RFC7464 has 11/2, RFC7838 has 29/2, RFC7932 has 55/2, RFC8305 has 27/0, RFC8336 has 13/1, RFC8441 has 8/2, RFC8878 has 0/7, RFC8999 has 5/0, RFC9002 has 63/1, RFC9204 has 42/2, RFC9209 has 11/0, RFC9211 has 4/0, RFC9218 has 41/1, RFC9220 has 1/0, RFC9221 has 16/0, RFC9287 has 8/0, RFC9292 has 5/1, RFC9297 has 43/0, RFC9298 has 67/0, RFC9368 has 45/0, RFC9369 has 15/0, RFC9406 has 7/0, RFC9412 has 0/0, RFC9438 has 19/1, RFC9530 has 5/3, RFC9651 has 28/1, RFC9841 has 10/0, RFC9842 has 26/0, RFC9931 has 5/0, draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers-11 has 28/0. `inventory_complete` is false; 17 RFC maps and 0 pinned maps remain incomplete. |

| Finding | Area | Status | Current evidence and closure condition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `PRE-001` | Public QUIC core contract | `Closed` | The public core is limited to the audited quic_core, client, server, config, diagnostics, and failure modules with opaque connections and streams; API snapshots and public loopback tests cover the supported transport lifecycle. Closure: Closed by the compiler-derived API audit, archive audit, and public-core behavior suites. |
| `PRE-002` | HTTP/3 package ownership | `Closed` | HTTP/3 sessions, QPACK, Capsules, and workers are owned by the http3 package while QUIC packet, TLS, UDP, Retry, token, and connection state remain core-owned. Closure: Closed by independent package builds, source/API boundary scans, compiled xref, and archive-content checks. |
| `PRE-003` | Connection isolation and admission | `Open` | Supervised connection actors, candidate admission, cancellation and cleanup have live regressions. New body-lifetime and idle-control findings show why prior closure cannot qualify changed source. Closure: Close only after current-source hostile-peer isolation, owner-death, cleanup and finite-resource evidence passes; complete platform and coverage matrices remain separately required. |
| `PRE-004` | Endpoint aggregate memory | `Open` | Admission and later receive/send/mailbox growth reserve memory before allocation. Typed pressure causes and bounded retry/release have new regressions; final-source aggregate-pressure evidence is pending. Closure: Regenerate current-source hostile-peer aggregate-memory, backpressure, parallel-progress, crash-release and client-refusal evidence before closing this finding. |
| `PRE-005` | Credential and mTLS platform matrix | `Open` | Scoped local credential suites cover certificate algorithms, mTLS, rotation, resumption and rejection. Cross-group and cookie-only HelloRetryRequest, ticket-age update and rollback, retry PSK binding and early-data rejection now have 104 scoped regressions and mutation checks; prior successes do not establish the complete current-source six-platform credential matrix. Closure: Collect current-source Ubuntu 24.04, macOS 15, and Windows 2025 attestations on OTP 28 and 29 and pass credential-matrix aggregate verification. |
| `PRE-006` | External atomic replay guard | `Closed` | The finite monitored adapter receives only a domain-separated fingerprint and retention interval; rejection, error, exit, and timeout fail closed to authenticated 1-RTT fallback without losing PSK resumption. Closure: Closed by direct adapter outcomes and public live accepted/rejected 0-RTT regressions. |
| `PRE-007` | qlog schema, breadth, and qvis compatibility | `Open` | Prior qlog execution predates the current source. The validator now binds capture start/end and trace digests to the complete source identity; the live current-source capture and qualification report must be regenerated. Closure: Regenerate a current-source Ready qlog-validate report with capture identity and retain writer failure/teardown evidence. |
| `PRE-008` | CUBIC differential and HyStart++ | `Open` | The deterministic oracle remains implemented. Current-source execution, all eight million-transition shards, and the independently validated aggregate are required before closing this finding. Closure: Run every declared current-source model shard and verify the complete million-transition aggregate. |
| `PRE-009` | Remaining automated qualification | `Open` | Static security, API/boundary, reproducible package, campaign, hostile/stability, qlog, model, examples, and OTP 29 release-simulation gates exist; coverage thresholds, complete RFC maps, expanded peers, cross-protocol performance, OTP 28, and canonical-archive qualification remain incomplete. Closure: Make every non-external source-candidate gate Ready and retain reproducible current-source evidence, including the adaptive coverage and raw capture artifacts. |
| `PRE-010` | HTTP/3 fixed-workload performance | `Open` | Historical fixed-workload successes and newer frozen diagnostic measurements have different source and host conditions. Every transition to `Ready` requires a retained Red failure, the bounded
implementation, and Green execution of the affected package plus every
upstream package. Package versions remain `0.1.0`. Tagging, publishing,
pushing, signing commits, and independent audit are not performed here.
